history.period: Ancient origins claimed; present structure 17th century (disputed)
history.summary: Hilltop temple on Chandranath Parvat above Paroda village, Quepem taluka, ~350 m elevation, reached by granite steps or a metalled road; Shiva worshipped as Chandreshwar ('Lord of the Moon') / Bhootnath, with a linga said to exude water droplets on full-moon nights. Dating is disputed: an ancient Sanskrit inscription claims nearly 2500 years and association with the Bhoja kings (whose capital Chandrapur, today's Chandor, was named after the deity); another source attributes the standing structure to the Kadamba period (~1050 CE); a third dates the present Goan-style building to the late 1600s around a rock-cut inner sanctum. DUPLICATE ROWS: CSV row 248 (same name, Sanguem) and row 230 ('Shri Chandreshwar Temple', Margao) almost certainly refer to this same shrine — dedupe recommended.

name: Shree Chandreshwar Bhootnath Temple
town_description: Paroda is a village in Quepem taluka, South Goa, at the foot of Chandranath hill. It is known for the hilltop Chandreshwar temple reached by granite steps or a metalled road, with views over Quepem and Chandor.

travel.road: ~14 km from Margao on the Margao-Quepem road; the temple arch (mahadwar) is visible from the main road. Granite steps or a metalled road lead to the hilltop.

visitor_information.best_time: October-February; early morning or evening (carry water for the climb)
